name: Elkanah
bio:
Elkanah was an Ephraimite from Ramathaim-Zophim, descended from Elihu, Tohu, and Zuph, who had two wives: Hannah and Peninnah. Peninnah had children, but Hannah was childless; each year Elkanah went up to Shiloh to sacrifice to the LORD, and always gave Hannah a double portion because he loved her, even though the LORD had closed her womb (1 Samuel 1:1-5).

When Hannah, repeatedly provoked by Peninnah over her childlessness, wept and would not eat, Elkanah comforted her, saying, "Why are you weeping? Why don't you eat? Why are you downhearted? Don't I mean more to you than ten sons?" (1 Samuel 1:8). After the LORD answered Hannah's prayer and she gave birth to Samuel, when Elkanah's household went up yearly to Shiloh to offer their sacrifice and fulfill Hannah's vow, Hannah stayed home until the child was weaned, and Elkanah agreed to her decision, saying, "Do what seems best to you... only may the LORD make good your word" (1 Samuel 1:21-23). Once Samuel was weaned, Hannah brought him to Shiloh and dedicated him to the LORD for life (1 Samuel 1:24-28).
